scope.built: the eclipse model with its brightness temperature (blackbody plus one band, isothermal skin); the Lambert phase curve with the Bond-albedo relation; synthetic data with a truth manifest; two instruments; two investigations
scope.notBuilt: transmission (X1 to X6, XR, XT and the whole-family size fail or are not measured at the gate), 205 spectra items, any published table (D1 to D3: no rights decision, nothing downloaded)

checks.bound: the new modules import every physical constant from the existing kernel constants (no numeric copy of k, h, c, sigma, the atomic mass unit, the AU or a solar or Jovian radius in them) and the constants they use equal astropy's CODATA 2018 and IAU 2015 values to a relative 1e-9

band-integrated Planck radiance against scipy.integrate.quad of the Planck function on 400 seeded points (T 200 to 10000 K, band edges 0.3 to 30 micron, widths at least 0.01 micron): relative error at most 1e-9; the integral over 0.001 to 100000 micron equals sigma T^4/pi to 1e-9 at five temperatures; the Rayleigh-Jeans limit holds to a relative 1e-3 at lambda T = 1e7 micron K (amended, see amendments); the band radiance is monotone in T

eclipse depth (Rp/Rs)^2 B(Tp)/B(T*) + Ag (Rp/a)^2 against an independent evaluation to a relative 1e-12 on 1,000 seeded points; the limits Tp = T* (depth (Rp/Rs)^2) and Ag = 0 (thermal only); monotone in Tp; the reflected term additive

the skin-slab band flux B(Tp) 2 E3(tau) + B(Tskin)(1 - 2 E3(tau)) against a numerical mu integral of the emergent intensity (scipy quad) at 300 seeded optical depths 1e-4 to 1e2: relative error at most 1e-9; tau = 0 gives B(Tp) exactly; the flux tends to B(Tskin) as tau grows; monotone in tau; Tskin = Tp/2^(1/4)

the Lambert phase function against the oracle's surface integral over the visible lit hemisphere (scipy dblquad) at 181 phase angles: absolute error at most 1e-8; Phi(0) = 1, Phi(pi/2) = 1/pi, Phi(pi) = 0 to 1e-12; the phase integral 2 integral Phi sin(alpha) d(alpha) = 3/2 to 1e-9; Ag = (2/3) AB and AB = (3/2) Ag round-trip to 1e-12; Phi monotone decreasing on [0, pi]

ensemble coverage: 2,000 seeded draws of a Lambert planet (Ag uniform 0.05 to 0.6, a/Rp 5 to 20), 24 phase-curve points uniform in alpha from 0.1 to 3.04 rad with Gaussian noise of 3 percent of the full-phase signal of Ag = 0.3 at that a/Rp, truth from the oracle's surface integral; the 95 percent interval of the least-squares albedo covers the truth in a fraction within [0.93, 0.97]

ensemble coverage: 2,000 seeded draws (Tp 800 to 2800 K, T* 4500 to 6500 K, Rp/Rs 0.05 to 0.15, band 3.6 to 4.5 micron, thermal depth with 5 percent Gaussian noise, truth from the oracle's quad); the 95 percent interval of the brightness temperature (propagated through the inverse band ratio) covers the truth in a fraction within [0.93, 0.97]; the round trip of the inverse is exact to 1e-9 without noise

misspecified phase curves: for a Lommel-Seeliger sphere and for Henyey-Greenstein single-scattering spheres with g = +0.3 and g = -0.3 (oracle truth, noise 2 percent of the full-phase signal, 24 points, 500 draws each) the Lambert fit is flagged as not describing the data (reduced chi-square above the 0.99 quantile, Wilson-Hilferty, and no albedo returned) in at least 80 percent of draws for each; for a true Lambert sphere the false flag rate is at most 2 percent of 500 draws

a band depth is refused as a brightness temperature when the reflected light of Ag = 0.3 is at least a tenth of the depth, and when the depth is at or below zero, and is converted otherwise: 30 seeded cases each side of the rule, all decided as the rule says

every one of 40 seeded hostile inputs (non-finite or non-positive temperature, mean molecular weight, gravity, radii, pressure, abundance, cross-section, band edges out of order, weights not summing to one, phase angle outside [0, pi], albedo outside [0, 1], optical depth below 0, outside the domain) refuses with a named reason and no number; and every result names its model and an assumes list that contains the words isothermal, one absorber, no scattering, no clouds and band-integrated (transmission), uniform blackbody and one skin (emission), Lambert (phase curve)

the scanner of the claim rule (forbidden English and Spanish patterns in the fixture) catches each of the 12 committed bad strings, passes each of the 6 committed permitted strings, and finds no violation in any string of js/i18n/en.atmospheres.js, js/i18n/es.atmospheres.js, the atmosphere sequences and their depths in both languages, and the prototype's own words

The synthetic eclipse-depth table and the synthetic phase curves are generated by a seeded function from the kernel (seed 202); each carries a truth manifest (the generating parameters, the noise standard deviation, the seed, the words "synthetic" and "no published table was compared"); the same seed gives identical bytes; a Lambert curve is recovered by fitAlbedo within its stated interval, a Lommel-Seeliger curve is flagged; the brightness temperature recovered from the synthetic eclipse depth covers the truth at the 95 percent interval. Numeric limits (stated before any run of the validator): over 2000 seeds the Lambert albedo interval covers in [0.93, 0.97], the Lommel-Seeliger curve is flagged in at least 0.8, the brightness-temperature interval covers in [0.93, 0.97]. These rows are the kernel on its own synthetic data, a consistency check and not an independent one.

The validation contract (Roadmap III 7.5.8e) asks for authentic data. None was available (D1 to D3 not measured: no rights decision, nothing downloaded). The row is recorded as not-measured, never as a pass, and the investigations carry the words "no published table was compared".

The gate bound (every plotted path vertex within 0.1 px of where its data is, the legend toggled from the keyboard, the keyboard readout in words, units in the axis titles, no drawing code outside js/plot/; jsdom) applied to the two plots of the slice (eclipse and phase); the gate counted three plots because it included the transmission panel, which is not built.

Bytes as the gate stated them for the eclipse and phase slice (kernel, two instruments, their words; the investigations are measured and reported separately because the gate bound them not): deferred at most 7,168 B gzipped, the kernel alone at most 2,282 B (Carl, AM3), no new lazy chunk, the first-visit precache added at most 64 B and the idle precache 0 B.
